$5x + 4y + 7z = \beta$
$175x + 194y + 57z = 361$
has infinitely many solutions, then $\alpha + \beta + 2$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

System of linear equations,

$7x + 11y + \alphaz = 13$
$5x + 4y + 7z = \beta$
$175x + 194y + 57z = 361$

Now we know that, for infinite solution~$D = {D}_{1} = {D}_{2} = {D}_{3} = 0$

Now solving~$D = 0$~we get,

~\left|$\begin{cases}7 & 11 & \alpha \\ 5 & 4 & 7 \\ 175 & 194 & 57\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

Now applying operation~${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - 25{R}_{1}$~we get,

\left|$\begin{cases}7 & 11 & \alpha \\ 5 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & - 81 & 57 - 25\alpha\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 81 ( 49 - 5\alpha ) + ( 57 - 25\alpha ) ( - 27 ) = 0$

$⇒ 270\alpha = - 2430 ⇒ \alpha = - 9$

And now solving~${D}_{1} = 0$~we get,

\left|$\begin{cases}13 & 11 & - 9 \\ \beta & 4 & 7 \\ 361 & 194 & 57\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(4 \times 57 - 7 \times 194\right) - \beta\left(11 \times 57 + 9 \times 194\right) + 361\left(11 \times 7 + 9 \times 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(- 1130\right) - \beta\left(2373\right) + 361\left(113\right) = 0$

$⇒ 13\left(- 10\right) - \beta\left(21\right) + 361 = 0$

$⇒ 21\beta = 231$

$⇒ \beta = 11$

$∴ \alpha + \beta + 2 = 4$

$

Given linear equations are&

$x + y + z = \alpha$

For this system of linear equations to have~inconsistent solution

$D = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2\alpha & 3 \\ 1 & 3\alpha & 5\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$= 1 + 17 - 11 \ne 0$

Hence, for~\alpha =$1& the system of equation has inconsistent solution.

questions.q:
Let $\lambda$ be a real number for which the system of linear equations

$x + y + z = 6,$

$4x + \lambday - \lambdaz = \lambda - 2$~and

$3x + 2y - 4z = - 5$

has infinitely many solutions. Then $\lambda$ is a root of the quadratic equation:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The system of equations& ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z + {d}_{1} = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z + {d}_{2} = 0$~and~${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z + {d}_{3} = 0$~have a infinitely many solution, if

$D = \left|$\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right| = 0, {D}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right| = 0, {D}_{2} = \left|$\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right| = 0$~and~${D}_{3} = \left|$\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}$\right| = 0 .$

Thus, for~infinitely many solutions, we have~$D = 0$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & \lambda & - \lambda \\ 3 & 2 & - 4\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(- 4\lambda + 2\lambda\right) - 1\left(- 16 + 3\lambda\right) + 1\left(8 - 3\lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 2\lambda + 16 - 3\lambda + 8 - 3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 24 - 3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 3$

And,~$\lambda = 3$ satisfies the equation ${λ}^{2} - \lambda - 6 = 0 .$

questions.q: Consider the system of linear equations $x + y + z = 5, x + 2y + {λ}^{2}z = 9$ and $x + 3y + \lambdaz = \mu$, where $\lambda, \mu \in R$. Then, which of the following statement is NOT correct ?
options: System has infinite number of solution if $\lambda = 1$ and $\mu = 13$
System has unique solution if $\lambda \ne 1$ and $\mu \ne 13$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$x + y + z = 5$

$x + 2y + {λ}^{2}z = 9$

$x + 3y + \lambdaz = \mu$

$⇒ △ = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & {λ}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & \lambda\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ △ = 2\lambda - 3{λ}^{2} - \lambda + {λ}^{2} + 1$

$⇒ △ = - 2{λ}^{2} + \lambda + 1$

We know that for infinite solutions, $△ = 0 & {△}_{1} = {△}_{2} = {△}_{3} = 0$

$⇒ - 2{λ}^{2} + \lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2{λ}^{2} - \lambda - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 1\right)\left(2\lambda + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1, \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Now, finding ${△}_{1}$ for $\lambda = 1$ we get,

${Δ}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & 1 \\ \mu & 3 & 1\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{1} = \mu - 13$

And for $\lambda = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$ we get,

${Δ}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & \dfrac{1}{4} \\ \mu & 3 & \dfrac{- 1}{2}\end{cases}$\right| = \dfrac{1}{4}\left|$\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 4 \\ 9 & 2 & 1 \\ \mu & 3 & - 2\end{cases}$\right| = \dfrac{7}{4}\left(13 - \mu\right)$

So, for $\lambda \ne 1 & \mu \ne 13$ system has no solution,

Hence, option \left(C\right)$ is the correct answer.

$

$△ = \left|$ egin{cases}2 & 4 & 2a \ 1 & 2 & 3 \ 2 & - 5 & 2\end{cases}$ ight|$

Hence, for~$a = 3, △ = 0$

Now finding,

${△}_{3} = \left|$ egin{cases}b & 2 & 4 \ 4 & 1 & 2 \ 8 & 2 & - 5\end{cases}$ ight|$

$⇒ {△}_{3} = 9 \left(b - 8 ight)$

So, for~$b = 8, {△}_{3} = 0$

Now solving~options we get,

For~$a = 8, b = 8, △ e 0, {△}_{3} = 0 ⇒$unique solution

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ be the real roots of the equation, $x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c = 0,$~($a, b, c \in R$ and $a, b \ne 0$). If the system of equations (in, $u, v, w$) given by $\alphau + \betav + \gammaw = 0, \betau + \gammav + \alphaw = 0, \gammau + \alphav + \betaw = 0$~has non-trivial solution, then the value of $\dfrac{a2}{b}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation& $x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c = 0$~has roots~$\alpha, \beta, \gamma$. Therefore,~

$\alpha + \beta + \gamma = - a$

$\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = b$

Since the given system of equations has non-trivial solutions,

we have~

\left|$\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & \gamma \\ \beta & \gamma & \alpha \\ \gamma & \alpha & \beta\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

or~${α}^{3} + {β}^{3} + {γ}^{3} - 3\alpha\beta\gamma = 0$

or~\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)\left[{α}^{2} + {β}^{2} + {γ}^{2} - \alpha\beta - \beta\gamma - \gamma\alpha\right] = 0$

or~\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)\left[\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)2 - 3\left(\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ - a\left[a^{2} - 3b\right] = 0$

or~$a^{2} / b = 3$

$

questions.q: The values of $\lambda$ and $\mu$ such that the system of equations $x + y + z = 6, 3x + 5y + 5z = 26$~and~$x + 2y + \lambdaz = \mu$ has no solution, are:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For the system of equations& ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = {d}_{1}, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = {d}_{2}$~and~${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = {d}_{3},$

We have~$D = \left|$ egin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$ ight|, {D}_{x} = \left|$ egin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$ ight|, {D}_{y} = \left|$ egin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$ ight|$~and~${D}_{z} = \left|$ egin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}$ ight| .$

And, the system has no solution, if~$D = 0$~and atleast one of~${D}_{x}, {D}_{y} ext{ and } {D}_{z}$~is non-zero.

Thus, for the given system of equations,

$x + y + z = 6,$~$3x + 5y + 5z = 26$~and~$x + 2y + \lambdaz = \mu$

We have~$D = \left|$ egin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \ 3 & 5 & 5 \ 1 & 2 & \lambda\end{cases}$ ight| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(5\lambda - 10 ight) - 1\left(3\lambda - 5 ight) + 1\left(6 - 5 ight) = 0$

$⇒ 5\lambda - 10 - 3\lambda + 5 + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2\lambda = 4$

$⇒ \lambda = 2 .$

And,~${D}_{z} = \left|$ egin{cases}1 & 1 & 6 \ 3 & 5 & 26 \ 1 & 2 & \mu\end{cases}$ ight| e 0$

$⇒ 1\left(5\mu - 52 ight) - 1\left(3\mu - 26 ight) + 6\left(6 - 5 ight) e 0$

$⇒ 5\mu - 52 - 3\mu + 26 + 6 e 0$

$⇒ 2\mu e 20$

$⇒ \mu e 10 .$

$∴$ For no solution $\lambda = 2$~and $\mu e 10 .$

questions.q: If the system of linear equations $x - 4y + 7z = g$; $3y - 5z = h$;~$- 2x + 5y - 9z = k$ is consistent, then:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$x - 4y + 7z = g$ ...(i)

$3y - 5z = h$ ...(ii)

$- 2x + 5y - 9z = k$ ...(iii)

(i) + (ii), we get

$x - y + 2z = g + h$ ...(iv)

(ii) - (iii), we get

$2x - 2y + 4z = h - k$

$⇒ x - y + 2z = \dfrac{h - k}{2}$ ...(v)

Since, coefficient of $x, y, z$ in (iv) and (v) are same. Hence, for system to be consistent

$g + h = \dfrac{h - k}{2}$

$⇒ 2g + 2h = h - k$

$⇒ 2g + h + k = 0$

questions.q: Let the system of equations $x + 2y + 3z = 5, 2x + 3y + z = 9, 4x + 3y + \lambdaz = \mu$ have infinite number of solutions. Then $\lambda + 2\mu$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $x + 2y + 3z = 5$, $2x + 3y + z = 9$ and $4x + 3y + \lambdaz = \mu$.

For infinite solutions, $\Delta = {Δ}_{1} = {Δ}_{2} = {Δ}_{3} = 0$.

$⇒ \Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & \lambda\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 3\lambda - 3 - 4\lambda + 8 + 18 - 36 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 13$

Now, finding

$⇒ {Δ}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}5 & 2 & 3 \\ 9 & 3 & 1 \\ \mu & 3 & - 13\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ \mu = 15$

Now, finding

$⇒ {Δ}_{2} = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 9 & 1 \\ 4 & \mu & \lambda\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{2} = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 9 & 1 \\ 4 & 15 & - 13\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{2} = 0$

And

$⇒ {Δ}_{3} = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 9 \\ 4 & 3 & \mu\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{3} = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 9 \\ 4 & 3 & 15\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{3} = 0$

For $\lambda = - 13, \mu = 15$ system of equation has infinite solutions.

$⇒ \lambda + 2\mu = 17$.

questions.q:
If the system of equations
$2x + y - z = 5$

$2x - 5y + \lambdaz = \mu$

$x + 2y - 5z = 7$
has infinitely many solutions, then$( \lambda + \mu{)}^{2} + ( \lambda - \mu{)}^{2}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given system of equations.

$2x + y - z = 5$

$2x - 5y + \lambdaz = \mu$

$x + 2y - 5z = 7$

For infinite solution $\Delta = 0 = {Δ}_{1} = {Δ}_{2} = {Δ}_{3}$

$⇒ \Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}2 & 1 & - 1 \\ 2 & - 5 & \lambda \\ 1 & 2 & - 5\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 51 - 3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 17$

$⇒ {Δ}_{3} = \left|$\begin{cases}5 & 2 & 1 \\ \mu & 2 & - 5 \\ 7 & 1 & 2\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ - 3 ( \mu + 13 ) = 0$

$⇒ \mu = - 13$

Now $( \lambda + \mu{)}^{2} + ( \lambda - \mu{)}^{2}$

$= ( 17 + 13{)}^{2} + ( 17 - 13{)}^{2}$

$= 900 + 16$

$= 916$

Hence this is the correct option.
